issues.legal_issue: An adoption by a widow can defeat the title of heirs who inherited property that originally belonged to the adoptive family, even when the property passed through a collateral before the adoption.
material_facts: The adoptive father died before his father, whose property later passed in equal shares to his two daughters.
One daughter inherited a share and, after her death, that share passed through her son to his sons, the appellants.
The widow of the adoptive father remained capable of adopting a son and eventually adopted the respondent.
The respondent claimed the property as property of his adoptive family; the appellants claimed through the daughter who had inherited it.
The court treated the inherited title as defeasible while the widow remained capable of adding a member to the coparcenary by adoption.
issues.conclusion: The adoption entitled the respondent to recover the property from the appellants, whose title derived through the collateral heir. The appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Hindu law, an adopted son's rights to the estate of his adoptive father relate back to the adoptive father's death. The estate remains the adoptive father's estate even when it has passed through a collateral, and an heir who takes while a widow remains capable of adopting takes a title defeasible on adoption. On adoption, that title and the titles of persons claiming under that heir are extinguished. This principle does not permit an adopted son to divest property belonging to a collateral in the collateral's own right. The Court applied Shrinivas Krishnarao Kango v. Narayan Devji Kango, discussed Amarendra Mansingh v. Sanatan Singh and Anant Bhikappa Patil v. Shankar Ramchandra Patil, and disapproved the contrary reasoning in Ramchandra Hanmant Kulkarni v. Balaji Datto Kulkarni.

rule.if: adopted_son_property_appeal and adoption_by_deceased_coparcener_widow and property_originated_in_adoptive_family and property_passed_through_collateral_heirs and widow_was_capable_of_adoption

predicates.adopted_son_property_appeal: The proceeding is an appeal concerning an adopted son's claim to recover property from persons claiming through earlier heirs.
predicates.adoption_by_deceased_coparcener_widow: A widow of a deceased member of the adoptive family adopted a son to her deceased husband.
predicates.property_originated_in_adoptive_family: The claimed property originally belonged to the adoptive family, rather than belonging to the collateral in the collateral's own right.
predicates.property_passed_through_collateral_heirs: The property passed by inheritance through a collateral and then to that collateral's heirs before the adoption.
predicates.widow_was_capable_of_adoption: Before the adoption, the widow remained capable of adding a son to the adoptive family by adoption.
predicates.adopted_son_can_recover_property_from_su: The adopted son can recover the property from successors whose title came through the collateral heir.

issues.definition: When an adopted-son property appeal concerns adoptive-family property inherited through collateral heirs while a widow remained capable of adoption, the rule produces the result that the adopted son can recover that property from those successors.
